cover.lede: How Sample looks, reads and moves. One file kept next to the code, so every screen we ship starts from the same decisions.
foundations.lede: What Sample is, how it should feel, and the three rules we reach for when two good ideas disagree.
foundations.product: Sample is the booking calendar for independent clinics. It turns a busy week of appointments into one calm screen a receptionist can read at a glance.
foundations.feel: Calm, because the people using it are busy. Exact, because a wrong time costs a patient a visit. Warm, because a clinic is a place of care.
foundations.principle-1-why: Every screen gives the week the most room. Menus and settings step back until someone needs them.
foundations.principle-2-why: A plain label beats a smart icon. If a control needs a tooltip to be understood, it needs a better word.
foundations.principle-3-why: One primary action per screen, one way to do each thing, one name for each idea across the product.
mark.lede: A soft square that holds the week, set beside the name. It signs the product; it never decorates it.
mark.lockup: The mark sits left of the wordmark, centered on its height. The gap between them is a third of the mark's width and never changes.
mark.sizes: Below 32 px the mark stands alone. The full lockup starts at 32 px, where the wordmark is still crisp.
mark.backgrounds: On the primary color the mark and the wordmark turn to the primary text color. Never place the mark on a photo or a pattern.
mark.clear-space: Keep clear space equal to the mark's corner radius, a quarter of its width, on every side. Nothing enters the dashed line: no text, no edge, no other logo.
color.lede: A warm paper neutral, one deep teal for action and a terracotta accent used sparingly. Every color is a token, and every token has a dark value.
color.primary-role: Teal is for the one action that matters on a screen and for the current place in the app. If everything is teal, nothing is.
color.accent-role: Terracotta marks what is new or needs a look today. Never a button, never a status.
color.neutral-role: Warm paper greys carry the page, so the schedule reads before the chrome around it.
typography.lede: A grotesque with a little warmth for headlines, a quiet sans for everything people read and click, and a mono for times and codes.
typography.display-role: Display. Page titles, empty states and the cover of a report. Never below 22 px.
typography.body-role: Body. Labels, tables, forms and messages: every word a person reads or clicks.
typography.mono-role: Mono. Times, durations and booking codes, anything that must line up in a column.
typography.sample-display: A calm week, at a glance
typography.sample-body: Dr. Rossi has two open slots this afternoon. Drag a booking to move it.
typography.sample-small: Reminders go out 24 hours before each visit.
typography.paragraph: Most of what Sample says is short: a name, a time, a room. When it has to say more, it says it in plain sentences that a tired receptionist can read at the end of a long day. Lines stay under seventy characters, paragraphs under four lines, and numbers always use the mono face so they line up.
spacing.lede: Space steps in fours: tight inside a control, generous between groups, so the week breathes without wasting a row.
spacing.rule: Space inside a control comes from steps 1 to 3, between controls from 4 and 6, between sections from 8 up. Never a number off the scale.
spacing.radii: Small for checkboxes and badges, medium for buttons and fields, large for cards and dialogs. Full is for switches and avatars only.
spacing.shadows: A shadow means something floats above the page. Cards sit flat on a hairline until a pointer lifts them.
spacing.borders: A hairline separates. A thicker line means focus or selection, and nothing else.
iconography.lede: Line icons on a 24 px grid, drawn with round ends, sized with the text they sit beside.
iconography.rule: Stroke 1.75 at 24 px, round caps and joins, no fills. Icons take the color of the text beside them and always come with a word, except in a toolbar where the word is the accessible label.
components.lede: Every control is built from the tokens above. Each one shows its states at rest, in light and in dark, so no state is designed in a hurry later.
components.button-primary: The one action that moves a booking forward. One per screen, labelled with a verb and its object.
components.button-secondary: Every other action that deserves a box: reschedule, export, invite. It can sit beside the primary or stand alone.
components.button-ghost: The quiet way out: cancel, skip, close. It lives next to a primary or a secondary, never on its own.
components.input: A visible label above, never a placeholder alone. The error says what to do, in words, beside an icon.
components.select: For a choice among five to fifteen known options. Fewer than five: show them as tabs or radios.
components.checkbox: A checkbox is saved with the form. A switch acts at once, so it never sits inside a form with a save button.
components.card: One appointment, one card. The time leads, the person follows, the status closes. A card lifts only when it can be opened.
components.table: For a day of bookings or a list of patients. Times in mono, status as a dot and a word, the current row marked by a bar.
components.tabs: To switch between views of the same thing. The selected tab carries a bar, never only a color.
components.dialog: Only to confirm what cannot be undone. The title asks the question, the buttons answer it in words.
components.toast: Says what just happened, in one line, and leaves after six seconds. An error stays until it is dismissed.
components.empty-state: Says why the space is empty and offers the one next step. No illustration, no joke.
components.nav: Four places at most, named with nouns. The current place is marked by its fill, and the mark always leads home.
motion.lede: Motion explains where something came from and nothing more. Short, eased out, and off when the system asks for less motion.
motion.fade: A new booking or a toast arrives from just below, in the slow step.
motion.expand: A row opens in place to show its details, in the base step.
motion.spinner: Only inside the button that started the wait, and only after half a second.
voice.lede: Sample speaks like a good receptionist: warm, brief and certain.
voice.tone-1: We name the person, the time and the place, every time.
voice.tone-2: We stay calm when something fails and say what to do next.
voice.tone-3: We use the words a clinic uses, not the words a database uses.
voice.dont-1: Success. Your appointment has been updated.
voice.dont-2: There may be availability later today.
voice.do-3: Reminder not sent. Check the phone number.
responsive.lede: Sample runs on a front desk monitor and on a clinician's phone between rooms. The layout changes at three widths; the rules below never do.
responsive.bp-640: Below 640 the week becomes a list of days and the menu folds behind a button.
responsive.bp-900: From 900 the sidebar stays open and the day shows two clinicians side by side.
responsive.bp-1200: From 1200 the week shows every clinician and the booking panel opens beside it.
